findings.issue: The test does not prove the after-commit part of CTO 5. rowVisibleAtSend calls credentials.existsById on the request thread. If sendEmail were moved inside the tx lambda, that call would join the open transaction, and Hibernate's AUTO flush would make the saved row visible, so the assertion would still pass. The production code is correct today (the send runs after tx.executeWithoutResult returns), but nothing guards that ordering against a regression.
findings.fix: In the doAnswer, record TransactionSynchronizationManager.isActualTransactionActive() and assert it is false. Or read the row through a REQUIRES_NEW TransactionTemplate or a separate JdbcTemplate connection, which cannot see uncommitted data.

findings.issue: CTO 1 asks for the 429 resend to be identical for taken and free numbers. The resend test compares only the status and the problem `code`. It does not compare the full problem body (title, detail, type) or the headers the way the 202 test does, so a branch-specific detail or header on the 429 path would go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Compare json(taken) with json(free) after removing per-request fields (instance, correlation id, timestamp), and compare comparableHeaders(taken) with comparableHeaders(free).

findings.issue: The ADR exists twice. The constitution (stage 4 and the knowledge table) puts ADRs in .openforge/knowledge/decisions/. The decisions README keeps docs/architecture/adr/ for platform-wide product ADRs, which are a separate numbering series. The docs copy already differs from the canonical record (lowercase 'accepted', different wording and refs), so the two will drift. Its number 0007 lines up with the OpenForge record only by coincidence: OpenForge 0005/0006 (deny-list, shared limits) are not mirrored, and docs 0005/0006 are payments and semantic search. tasks.md T7 also named a path that does not exist (docs/adr/), and its grep for 'Accepted' would not match this copy.
findings.fix: Keep one canonical record. Preferred: delete the docs copy and point api.md and auth-service.md at the api.md section, or describe the decision inline. If the Owner wants product-facing ADRs for auth contract changes, keep the docs copy as the product ADR, state that it uses the docs numbering series, and reduce .openforge/knowledge/decisions/0007 to a pointer so the text is not duplicated.

findings.issue: getConnection() in setUp is never closed, so each test leaks a connection.
findings.fix: Use try-with-resources on the RedisConnection, or call redis.execute(c -> { c.serverCommands().flushAll(); return null; }).

findings.issue: The WARN throttle reads System.currentTimeMillis() directly, while the service elsewhere uses the TimeProvider abstraction. The notifier also resolves the owner with findWithRolesByPhoneAndPhoneVerifiedTrue, which fetches roles it never uses.
findings.fix: Optional: inject TimeProvider for the throttle clock. A plain verified-phone lookup would avoid the role join, but reusing the existing query is acceptable.

summary: The change does what the design and the 7 CTO conditions require. addPhone runs the same query, changePhone, issueCode and 30 s cooldown for taken and free numbers, and only the last fire-and-forget hand-off differs: sendSms for a free number, claimNotifier.attempted for a taken one. The integration test asserts 202, an empty body and identical headers, no SMS for the taken number, and 429 AUTH_RATE_LIMITED on resend in both cases. The resend check could be stricter (minor). PhoneClaimNotifier uses an atomic setIfAbsent with the window TTL on an owner-UUID key (no phone in Redis). It runs off-thread, catches every RuntimeException and throttles the WARN with a CAS. A real-Redis Testcontainers test proves exactly one email from 20 concurrent calls, a TTL of about 24 h, a new notice after the key is deleted, and no throw, no email and a single WARN when Redis is down (CTO 2). The verify re-check and the DataIntegrityViolation mapping both stay and now return AUTH_OTP_INVALID. Unit tests cover both, and integration tests cover the decoy code, the lost race and the unique index directly (CTO 3). The storefront hint is neutral and tested (CTO 4). PASSWORD_SET is sent only when the reset created the credential, after the tx returns, inside a try/catch. The tests assert the row, the exact email, no email for password users, and fail-open behaviour; the after-commit assertion itself is weak (minor) (CTO 5). The diff does not touch docs/techdebt. AC-12(b)'s 'techdebt entry' wording was waived by the CTO under condition 6 and deferred to the register-sync objective, so AC-12 counts as met (CTO 6). The deploy order is documented in the ADR and auth-service.md (CTO 7). No AUTH_PHONE_TAKEN emission remains, and no earlier tests were deleted. The repo has no existing throttled-log or SET NX helper this code should have reused, and the per-class virtual-thread executor follows NotificationGateway and AuthAuditPublisher. On the ADR question: copying it into docs/architecture/adr is not appropriate as a duplicate. The constitution puts ADRs in .openforge/knowledge/decisions, the docs series has its own numbering, and the two copies already differ. There should be one canonical record (minor). No blocker or major findings, so: approve.
